% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.classical
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The BFGS update, secant equation, positive-definiteness preservation and determinant identity are classical. Trace/determinant analysis is developed in Nocedal~\cite[Section~5, equations (5.7), (5.15) and (5.21)]{FND_N92} and the earlier Byrd--Nocedal work~\cite{FND_BN89}. The determinant endpoint below belongs to that established theory. The complete adjacent-degree principal-minor inequality is distinguished from it; the literature audit found no exact match, without establishing publication priority. Gram determinants, Schur complements and Cauchy--Binet are standard tools.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.classical

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.products
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Product bounds and arithmetic--geometric mean already occur in BFGS convergence proofs: see Sch\"opfer~\cite[proof of Theorem~3.7]{S16} and Jin--Jiang--Mokhtari~\cite[Appendices C--D]{FND_JJM24AW}. Their smooth hypotheses and normalized quantities differ from those below. Here the actual principal-minor hierarchy supplies reciprocal bounds for $q_k=g_k^TH_kg_k$, including the finite-horizon and summable-decrease conclusions; those specific conclusions were not located in the accessed literature.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.products

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.energy
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The energy cancellations below are algebraic consequences of the classical Hessian update~\cite[Section~5]{FND_N92}; congruence and quadratic-form inequalities are established tools. Their use in a moving-frame criterion still requires the separately stated visibility, secant and transport hypotheses.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.energy

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.residual
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Summable multiplicative-error estimates and normalization have precedents in Combettes--V\~u~\cite[Lemmas 2.2--2.3]{FND_CV13}. The argument below additionally derives the restricted trace bound and an $O(N^2)$ cumulative allowance. Its additive errors need not be summable, so the earlier lemmas alone do not prove this residual theorem.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.residual

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION T.certificate
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
This is a sufficient condition for ordinary full BFGS. Multiplicative-error normalization is an established technique~\cite[Lemmas 2.2--2.3]{FND_CV13}, also used in the rescaling discussion below and Module G. The comparison field here may be singular and unbounded, and transport is projected away from the step. Consequently a uniformly coercive, bounded variable-metric convergence theorem does not supply this result or its objective-pair quantifiers.
% END ATTRIBUTION T.certificate

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION R.bregman
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The Bregman expression uses established terminology~\cite[Definition~1]{BB} and ordinary supporting-plane calculus. Only its supporting endpoint must be differentiable; no new divergence construction is asserted.
% END ATTRIBUTION R.bregman

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION R.norms
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Full-BFGS convergence on the Euclidean norm in arbitrary dimension was established by Guo--Lewis~\cite[Corollary~4.2]{GL18}; scalar absolute-value convergence appears in Lewis--Overton~\cite[Section~5.1]{LO}. These are known cases recovered here. The wider gauge and mixed-power conclusions use the radial argument under the stated minimizer and compact-basin hypotheses.
% END ATTRIBUTION R.norms

anchor: \subsection{A common spectral regularizer not automatically covered}
text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION R.spectral
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The optimizer in this example is a specialization of singular-value thresholding~\cite[Theorem~2.1]{CCS10}. That standard calculation is separate from the rotated-pair obstruction to the radial condition established below; the obstruction makes no claim of BFGS failure.
% END ATTRIBUTION R.spectral

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.centered
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Guo--Lewis~\cite[Theorem~4.1 and Corollary~4.4]{GL18} uses smooth extension and proves a weaker subsequential conclusion for $u^2+|v|$. The theorem below gives full convergence for that example within its centered family. Its smooth secant estimate uses established cocoercivity~\cite[Theorem~2.5]{WW}: local regularity is used on an open convex neighborhood, with compact buffers and, where needed, an enlarged constant. It does not require a globally Lipschitz gradient or minimization of each original summand at the center.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.centered

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.fiber
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Invertible affine invariance is established in Lewis--Overton~\cite[Section~2]{LO} and Xie--W\"achter~\cite[Theorem~II.1]{XW}. The rectangular reduction below additionally identifies the point selected on an affine fiber. Sch\"opfer's smooth noncompact convergence results~\cite[Theorems 3.4 and 3.7]{S16} do not identify that selector. Exact publication priority for this formula remains unresolved; no originality claim is made.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.fiber

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.rates
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Related quantitative work includes smooth strongly convex Armijo--Wolfe rates~\cite{FND_JJM24AW}, smooth exact-search rates~\cite{FND_JJM26EX}, and smooth self-concordant analysis~\cite{FND_JM25}. These assumptions and line searches differ from the nonsmooth settings below. Their matrix-potential techniques are precedents, but their rate theorems do not imply these estimates. The present rates count accepted iterations, with no uniform bound on line-search trials.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.rates

anchor: \section{Matrix limits and line-search existence are different questions}
text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.lines
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Lewis--Overton~\cite[Theorem~4.5 and Proposition~4.11]{LO} supplies scalar Armijo--weak-Wolfe existence theory. Differentiability of the restriction to a ray does not imply full-space differentiability at acceptance. The existence argument and the finite obstruction below preserve that distinction; neither asserts an infinite-run failure.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.lines

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION H.norm
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The Euclidean-norm consequence is already Guo--Lewis~\cite[Corollary~4.2]{GL18}, and the scalar absolute-value case is established in Lewis--Overton~\cite[Section~5.1]{LO}. The theorem here treats the larger finite convex homogeneous class without assuming bounded iterates.
% END ATTRIBUTION H.norm

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION H.twopiece
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The precise prior result is Xie--W\"achter's 2017 preprint~\cite[Theorem~IV.1]{XW}. Its finite detection of unbounded descent in the two-piece model is stronger there than the infinite-run value conclusion proved here for the many-piece family.
% END ATTRIBUTION H.twopiece

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION H.selector
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The invariant-subspace argument extends the affine-invariance background~\cite[Theorem~II.1]{XW}. Exact prior publication of the resulting $H_0^{-1}$-metric selector for this noncompact homogeneous class remains unresolved, as for Module F's rectangular lifting formula. This uncertainty concerns attribution, not an additional hypothesis of the theorem.
% END ATTRIBUTION H.selector
